> In if (opt$meanstructure == "default") { :
>    the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
> Could anyone give me some suggestions please? Thank you very much.

Yes, you need to 'name' all your argument in the 'sem()' call (except
the first, which is always the model). So this should work:

fit=sem(model,data=empaper2,missing="ml")

If you do not explicitly use 'data=', R will assign empaper2 to whatever
is defined as the second argument in the function. These are the
arguments for sem:

args(lavaan:::sem)
function (model = NULL, meanstructure = "default", fixed.x = "default",
     orthogonal = FALSE, std.lv <http://std.lv> = FALSE, data = NULL, std.ov = FALSE,
     missing = "default", ordered = NULL, sample.cov = NULL, sample.mean
= NULL,
     sample.nobs = NULL, group = NULL, group.label = NULL, group.equal =
"",
     group.partial = "", cluster = NULL, constraints = "", estimator =
"default",
     likelihood = "default", information = "default", se = "default",
     test = "default", bootstrap = 1000L, mimic = "default",
representation = "default",
     do.fit = TRUE, control = list(), WLS.V = NULL, NACOV = NULL,
     start = "default", verbose = FALSE, warn = TRUE, debug = FALSE)
NULL

The second one is 'meanstructure'. So you inadvertently assigned your
data.frame (empaper2) to the 'meanstructure' argument, and hence lavaan
complained with the error:

Error in setLavaanOptions(opt) :
   meanstructure must be TRUE, FALSE or "default"

However, I get this question so often, I'm seriously considering
changing the order of the arguments so that 'data' is actually the
second one.

Yves.

On 11/07/2012 09:47 PM, Dr. Hans Hansen wrote:

Well, suppose 'HS.model' contains the model syntax, and 'HS.missing'
contains missing data, something very rudimentary could be this (using
the 'mice' package):

# generate 5 multiple complete datasets
out <- mice(HS.missing, m=5)
D1 <- complete(out, 1)
D2 <- complete(out, 2)
D3 <- complete(out, 3)
D4 <- complete(out, 4)
D5 <- complete(out, 5)

# fit model for each complete dataset
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model, data=D1)
fit2 <- cfa(HS.model, data=D2)
fit3 <- cfa(HS.model, data=D3)
fit4 <- cfa(HS.model, data=D4)
fit5 <- cfa(HS.model, data=D5)

# predict scores for all models
p1 <- predict(fit1)
p2 <- predict(fit2)
p3 <- predict(fit3)
p4 <- predict(fit4)
p5 <- predict(fit5)

# compute 'average' across 5 sets of scores:
scores <- (p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5)/5

Hope this helps,

Yves.

You have separate regression coefficient per group. So there is no
single 'a' or 'b' or 'c', but you have 'a1,a2,a3', 'b1,b2,b3' and
'c1,c2,c3'.

You can adapt your syntax as follows:

Y ~ c(c1,c2,c3)*X + c(b1,b2,b3)*M
M ~ c(a1,a2,a3)*X
...
ab1 := a1*b1
ab2 := a2*b2
ab3 := a3*b3

tot1 := c1 + (a1*b1)
tot2 := c2 + (a2*b2)
tot3 := c3 + (a3*b3)

Hope this helps,

messages.subject: Re: two-group “added growth” LGM?
messages.body_plain:
Greg,

I haven't run a model like this before, but it should be easy enough.  If a parameter is constrained to equality across groups, you only need to label that parameter once (see "intercept" and "slope" below), but for different parameters for each group, you can use the c() function to constrain (or NA/label, if free) the parameter for each group.  Here, I am forcing the loadings onto the "added" growth slope to be zero for the first group, but 0-1-2-3 for the second group (or use whatever values you would use for the "slope" loadings).  I imagine you would also fix the (co)variance to zero in the first group, since they are in effect "missing" that construct altogether.

addGrowth <- "
         intercept =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
         slope =~ 0*t1 + 1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4
         added =~ c(0, 0)*t1 + c(0, 1)*t2 + c(0, 2)*t3 + c(0, 3)*t4

         ## change NA to 0 if you do not want the "added" growth slope to be correlated with the common intercept/slope
         added ~~ c(0, NA)*added + c(0, NA)*intercept + c(0, NA)*slope

          ## use a single label for a free parameter to constrain across groups.  It works the same as: intercept ~~ c(psi11, psi11)*intercept
         intercept ~~ psi11*intercept + psi21*slope
         slope ~~ psi22*slope
"

The documentation available on the lavaan site has a PDF and a link to Yves' article in the Journal of Statistical Software, both of which demonstrate model syntax for multiple groups.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/?q=node/14

Terry

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Hans,

I think fit indices are one way to evaluate model fit. I know that many groups of researchers are trying to improve the way that fit indices are currently used or find the alternative methods for model fit evaluation. One example is Saris, Satorra, and van der Weld (2009) approach to find a model misspecification by modification indices and power to detect nontrivial misfits in modification indices. This is very interesting approach and the miPowerFit function is available in the semTools package. Addition fit indices are available in the moreFitIndices function in that package too.

For my personal perspective on fit indices, I think that it reflects the belief that hypothesized model do not replicate the model underlying the data and fit indices are designed to capture how well this hypothesized model approximates the relations among variables in the data. Regardless of good or bad model fit, I think we should look at the fit at parameter levels because a good model fit does not mean that the hypothesized model is corrected. Like philosophy of science, we should gather information of model fit from various sources to justify whether the hypothesized model should be the one.

Sunthud

This is a bug (only triggered if 1) missing="ml", 2) the model contains
exogenous variables). Fixed now in the dev version (and the SE are not

install.packages("pbivnorm")

regression are categorical, with more than two levels. Lavaan (unlike
lm())) does NOT automatically expand categorical predictors to a set of
dummy variables. You need to create dummy variables manually.

On 11/27/2012 03:49 PM, Bill Shipley wrote:
> Hello.  After fitting an SEM I can successfully obtain the

> resid(out,type="standardized") Most of the values are NA.  I don't know
> why this occurs or how to solve it.  Can anyone point me in the right
> direction?

The 'standardized' residuals in lavaan are not the same as those
computed by EQS or LISREL. They are the same as those computed by Mplus.
The formulas can be found in this document (from the Mplus website):

http://www.statmodel.com/download/StandardizedResiduals.pdf

The last paragraph in that document explains the 'NA' problem:

"One problem with Hausman's (1978) approach to computing the residual
variance is that sometimes the variance estimates given by (14) and (16)
can be negative. In that case the standardized residual is not computed
and Mplus prints 999. Typically in such situation the normalized
residual can be used."

Note that you can also use

resid(out, type="cor"), to get residuals in a correlation metric.

Yves.
